title: Information Protection, Data Lifecycle and Governance

header.html: Describe data classification capabilities; Describe the value of content explorer and activity explorer; Describe sensitivity labels and sensitivity label policies; Describe data loss prevention (DLP); Describe records management; Describe retention policies, retention labels and retention label policies
the official SC-900 study guide, skills measured as of October 21, 2026

html:
1The data protection journey

Microsoft Purview protects data in four steps: know it, protect it, prevent loss, and govern it over time.

Step Capability
Know your data Data classification, content explorer, activity explorer
Protect your data Sensitivity labels and policies, encryption
Prevent data loss Data loss prevention (DLP)
Govern your data Retention, records management

2Data classification

Data classification finds and labels data by type and sensitivity.

Classifier How it identifies
Sensitive information types (SITs) Patterns such as credit card or national ID numbers, using patterns, keywords and checksums
Trainable classifiers Machine learning models that learn what a document type looks like (for example contracts)
Exact data match (EDM) Match against your own sensitive data in a table
Exam tip

. Credit card numbers = sensitive information type. "Documents that look like resumes or contracts" = trainable classifier.

3Content explorer and activity explorer

Tool Shows Question
Content explorer The actual items (files, emails) that carry sensitivity labels, retention labels or sensitive info types, with their location and content What is labeled, and where is it?
Activity explorer What happened to labeled content: label changes, file copies, shares, DLP matches over time What activity is occurring?

Exam tip

. Content explorer = the "what and where". Activity explorer = the "who did what and when". Both are in the Purview portal and need appropriate roles.

4Sensitivity labels and policies

A sensitivity label is a tag that classifies and protects a file or email. The label travels with the content.

Label action Example
Encryption Only named people can open the file
Content marking Header, footer, watermark such as "Confidential"
Access restrictions Control who can copy, print, forward
Scope Files, emails, Teams, SharePoint sites and groups, and more
Term Meaning
Sensitivity label The tag and its protections
Sensitivity label policy Publishes labels to chosen users or groups and sets rules such as mandatory labeling, default label and justification for downgrade

Labels can be applied manually by users or automatically when content matches a sensitive information type.

Exam tip

. Label = the tag and protection. Label policy = who gets which labels and the rules for using them. A label does nothing for a user until it is published in a policy.

5Data loss prevention (DLP)

DLP identifies, monitors and protects sensitive information to stop it leaving the organization by accident or on purpose.

Item Details
Locations Exchange email, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, Windows and macOS endpoints, and more
Conditions Content contains a sensitive info type, a label, or is shared externally
Actions Block, warn (policy tip with override), audit only, notify
Tips Policy tips teach users why an action is risky

Example: block email that contains a credit card number sent to an external address, and notify the sender.

Exam tip

. DLP = prevent sensitive data from leaving (email, share, copy to USB). Sensitivity labels = classify and protect the content. They work together.

6Retention and records management

Data lifecycle management keeps what you need and removes what you do not.

Tool What it does
Retention policy Applies broadly to locations (all mailboxes, a site) to retain, delete, or retain then delete
Retention label Applied to individual items; the label travels with the item and can start retention from an event or declare a record
Retention label policy Publishes retention labels to users or applies them automatically
Records management Marks items as records or regulatory records so they are immutable (cannot be edited or deleted by users), with file plan, disposition review and proof of disposal

Whichever retain rule applies, the item is kept; retention wins over deletion if both apply. [Verify live]

Exam tip

. Policy = broad, location-based. Label = per item and follows the file. Record = locked so it cannot be changed or deleted. Retention label policy = how labels are published to users.

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors wants to stop emails containing credit card numbers from being sent externally. Which solution fits?

  • AAccess reviews
  • BData loss prevention
  • CAzure Bastion
  • DSafe Links
Show the answer

Answer: B. DLP can block or warn on sensitive information leaving the organization.

S2Which tool shows the actual files that have a particular sensitivity label and where they are stored?

  • AActivity explorer
  • BSecure score
  • CSentinel workbook
  • DContent explorer
Show the answer

Answer: D. Content explorer lists labeled items and their locations.

S3An admin wants to see how many times labeled files were copied or shared last month. Which tool?

  • AActivity explorer
  • BContent explorer for labeled items
  • CCompliance score for improvement actions
  • DKey Vault for secrets and keys
Show the answer

Answer: A. Activity explorer shows actions taken on labeled content over time.

S4What makes sensitivity labels available to chosen users?

  • AA retention policy
  • BA sensitivity label policy
  • CA DLP alert
  • DA Conditional Access policy
Show the answer

Answer: B. Label policies publish labels to users or groups.

S5A company wants to keep all Exchange mailboxes for seven years, then delete. Which tool fits best?

  • AA retention policy
  • BA trainable classifier
  • CAn NSG
  • DA sensitivity label
Show the answer

Answer: A. Retention policies apply broadly to locations to retain and delete.

S6What does declaring an item a record do?

  • AEncrypts it with a key stored in Azure Key Vault for the owner
  • BLocks it so it cannot be edited or deleted by users
  • CMoves it to Azure Bastion for safe remote access by administrators
  • DMarks it as risky and sends an alert to the security team
Show the answer

Answer: B. Records are immutable under records management.

7.2 Recall questions

R1Name the three classifier types.

Show the answer

Sensitive information types, trainable classifiers and exact data match.

R2What does a sensitivity label do?

Show the answer

Classifies and protects content with encryption, markings and access limits.

R3What does DLP stand for?

Show the answer

Data loss prevention.

R4What is the difference between a retention policy and label?

Show the answer

A policy applies broadly to locations; a label applies to individual items.

R5What is a regulatory record?

Show the answer

A stricter record that nobody can alter or remove, including administrators.

R6Which explorer shows activity over time?

Show the answer

Activity explorer.

8Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Classification sensitive information types, trainable classifiers, exact data match
Explorers content explorer = what and where; activity explorer = what happened
Sensitivity labels encryption, markings, access limits; label policy publishes them
DLP blocks or warns on sensitive data leaving; email, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, endpoints
Retention and records retention policy broad; retention label per item and publishes via label policy; records are locked
